install_tell: docker run -p 8000:8000 chromadb/chroma  (or: pip install chromadb && chroma run --path /chroma/data)
misconfig_patterns: Chroma ships auth OFF by default (token/basic auth is an external Envoy/proxy add-on) so collection-list, heartbeat, and any co-served persist-dir tarball are reachable unauthenticated out of the box
A 'backup' is the filesystem persist dir (chroma.sqlite3 + HNSW .bin index files) or a chromadb-ops snapshot, sometimes served as a static tarball next to the API

AI-scope discriminator: a bare served chroma.sqlite3 / .tar.gz is GENERIC SQLITE SUBSTRATE until confirmed to carry vector/AI data. AI-scope CONFIRMED when GET .../collections returns objects carrying a configuration_json/configuration block with an 'hnsw' key (space=cosine/l2/ip, ef/M) and/or a non-empty embedding_function, AND the persist dir/tarball listing shows the HNSW companion files (data_level0.bin, header.bin, link_lists.bin, length.bin) alongside chroma.sqlite3. SQLite tables embeddings/embedding_metadata/segments/collections (names-only) are the secondary confirmer. A tarball with only chroma.sqlite3 and no .bin index, no embeddings table, no collection dimension = generic SQLite, OUT of scope.

Restraint: names and metadata are the finding. Listing collections, reading heartbeat/version/pre-flight, and reading a static directory listing of a served persist dir are read-only enumeration and permitted. DOWNLOADING a served chroma.sqlite3 or backup tarball is exfiltration of the embedded vectors/metadata, forbidden. POSTing to /collections (the CVE-2026-45829 embedding_function vector) is a write/RCE primitive, forbidden on the survey set. Do not GET /collections/{id}/get or /query to pull embeddings/documents; the collection list alone proves the vector store.

response_markers: The v1 API is deprecated. Please use /v2 apis
active_probe.false_positive_check: Broad http.title dorks miss it: ChromaDB FastAPI serves no HTML title at / (404 JSON or redirect) so any title match is a different service on 8000. Anchor on the JSON body field 'nanosecond heartbeat' from /api/v2/heartbeat (vendor-unique) AND a 200 on /api/v2/version returning a bare semver; uvicorn alone 404s both. Rust-frontend Chroma (chroma run / Chroma Cloud) answers heartbeat identically but is NOT the vulnerable Python FastAPI path — distinguish by Server header (hyper/axum vs uvicorn); tag Rust frontends as CANDIDATE-only. A served chroma.sqlite3/*.tar.gz behind nginx autoindex/SimpleHTTPServer with NO live heartbeat is a generic exposed-file finding, not this API surface. 410 Gone on /api/v1/collections (body 'The v1 API is deprecated') is itself a positive Chroma>=1.0.0 fingerprint — pivot to the v2 path, do not discard. LBot/catch-all: require the exact integer-valued 'nanosecond heartbeat' JSON shape plus a matching semver, treat a 200 on a random nonsense path as a catch-all FP.

deployment_tells: GET /api/v2/heartbeat returns {"nanosecond heartbeat": <int>} — vendor-unique liveness signal
GET /api/v1/collections returns 410 'The v1 API is deprecated' on Chroma >= 1.0.0 (positive fingerprint, pivot to v2)
Co-located static file server serving chroma.sqlite3 + HNSW .bin companions (data_level0.bin/header.bin/link_lists.bin) = the persist-dir backup
pivot_paths: GET /api/v2/heartbeat -> confirm live Chroma + capture nanosecond heartbeat (liveness, no auth)
GET /api/v2/version -> read semver to CVE-scope (1.0.0-1.5.8 => CVE-2026-45829 surface; <1.0.0 => v1 API path)
GET /api/v2/pre-flight-checks -> read max_batch_size and supported features (server config, names-only)

GET /api/v2/tenants/default_tenant/databases/default_database/collections -> LIST collection objects: names, ids, metadata, hnsw configuration. This is the snapshot/backup contents index without touching files
GET .../collections_count -> count of collections (scale of the backup)
If pre-1.0.0: GET /api/v1/collections for the equivalent list; a 410 confirms >=1.0.0 and you pivot to v2

Enumerate co-located static file server (nginx autoindex / SimpleHTTPServer) for a served chroma.sqlite3 or *.tar.gz backup -> read the DIRECTORY LISTING only (file names, sizes, .bin index presence) to confirm a vector persist dir. Names confirm scope; stop there
vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-45829: ChromaToast — pre-auth RCE (CVSS 10.0) in the Python FastAPI server; embedding_function config in a POST to /api/v2/tenants/{tenant}/databases/{db}/collections fetches+executes a Hugging Face model via trust_remote_code BEFORE the auth check fires; affects 1.0.0-1.5.8; Rust frontend and local-only deploys unaffected; ~73% of internet-exposed instances vulnerable; leaks files/secrets the server can read incl. the entire persist dir/backup

CVE-2024-37032-class (no native auth): not a Chroma CVE per se but the governing exposure — Chroma ships auth OFF by default, so collection-list, heartbeat, and any co-served persist-dir tarball are reachable unauthenticated out of the box
